matches.match_basis: DOI, full title, five ordered authors, year and original-specific empirical fingerprints agree.

all_shipped_match_analysis.alias_analysis: Exact original DOI is printed in Archer 2015 and the deposited current reference array; baseline title/authors/year match. No identifier alias is needed to establish representation.
all_shipped_match_analysis.alternate_report_analysis: Archer 2015 reports the 2014 national sample of 3,658. DeWitt 2016 explicitly reuses that national sample and index, but also analyses a distinct 2014-15 targeted sample of 6,861 from 18 schools. For the reused national sample, distribution and demographic results are repeat reporting, not a second independent dataset. However, DeWitt 2016 independently reports the same low/high distribution and South Asian/high-cultural-capital/top-set pattern in its targeted sample as well. Current Results explicitly attributes the younger-cohort distribution to BOTH papers, and Discussion explicitly places BOTH in the retested set. Its new 7,013-person survey measures the corresponding distribution and demographic pattern. Therefore the 2016 report is an empirically tested original paper, not merely the source of an instrument or an alternate title/version of the 2015 article. No claim is made that every 2016 analysis is retested.

decisions.rationale: Author 2 et al. (2015) binds to Archer, Dawson, DeWitt, Seakins and Wong: the current paper repeats the 14-item index, national younger-sample gender composition, 27.2% low/67.6% medium distribution, demographic/setting patterns, and especially the distinctive 37% versus 9% high/low-science-capital A-level aspiration comparison printed in Archer 2015 Table 2. The complete deposited bibliography identifies this paper, while its other Archer 2015 entry is the Black-students/parents paper, not this index-and-national-survey report. This is joint bibliography plus original-specific empirical fingerprint evidence, not a year match. The sole shipped counterpart is this exact original; exporting target 0 again would duplicate row 5.
decisions.strongest_contrary_evidence: Previously an anonymized 2015 self-citation could not be equated with shipped Archer 2015. This remains valid history, but the new bibliography and exact original empirical fingerprints now close that identity gap.

actual_empirical_retest.original_finding: Younger students’ science capital is unevenly distributed/patterned by demographic characteristics and science set, and higher capital relates to A-level/university science aspirations.
actual_empirical_retest.current_corresponding_analysis: New age-17/18 survey distribution, gender/ethnicity/cultural-capital/set comparisons, A-level course enrolment and post-18 university intentions.

evaluated_counterparts.relationship: Related earlier report with shared 2014 national dataset, not a DOI/title/version alias and not an exhaustive representation of the 2016 report’s tested targeted-sample finding.

all_shipped_match_analysis.alias_analysis: The supplied complete counterpart list and root baseline contain only Archer 2015. Bibliography and full frontmatter identify two journal reports with different author lists and titles. Distinctness is additionally grounded in the 2016 report’s 6,861-person targeted sample and new analyses, not DOI/year difference. No supplied alias maps DeWitt 2016 to row 5.

DeWitt 2016 explicitly reuses that national sample and index, but also analyses a distinct 2014-15 targeted sample of 6,861 from 18 schools. For the reused national sample, distribution and demographic results are repeat reporting, not a second independent dataset. However, DeWitt 2016 independently reports the same low/high distribution and South Asian/high-cultural-capital/top-set pattern in its targeted sample as well. Current Results explicitly attributes the younger-cohort distribution to BOTH papers, and Discussion explicitly places BOTH in the retested set. Its new 7,013-person survey measures the corresponding distribution and demographic pattern. Therefore the 2016 report is an empirically tested original paper, not merely the source of an instrument or an alternate title/version of the 2015 article. No claim is made that every 2016 analysis is retested.
all_shipped_match_analysis.closest_chain_analysis: The current paper directly attributes tested younger-cohort findings to both papers. DeWitt 2016 is not an intervening report that removes the directly named Archer 2015 aspiration finding; Archer 2015 is not merely an ancestor for that separately attributed current comparison. Conversely, re-reporting the national sample does not exhaust DeWitt 2016 because its targeted-sample distribution/pattern is also inside the directly attributed retested set. Count original papers with an actually retested finding, not independent tests or every dataset.

decisions.rationale: Archer 2015 reports the 2014 national sample of 3,658. DeWitt 2016 explicitly reuses that national sample and index, but also analyses a distinct 2014-15 targeted sample of 6,861 from 18 schools. For the reused national sample, distribution and demographic results are repeat reporting, not a second independent dataset. However, DeWitt 2016 independently reports the same low/high distribution and South Asian/high-cultural-capital/top-set pattern in its targeted sample as well. Current Results explicitly attributes the younger-cohort distribution to BOTH papers, and Discussion explicitly places BOTH in the retested set. Its new 7,013-person survey measures the corresponding distribution and demographic pattern. Therefore the 2016 report is an empirically tested original paper, not merely the source of an instrument or an alternate title/version of the 2015 article. No claim is made that every 2016 analysis is retested. All supplied shipped counterparts and the root baseline have been checked: none represents this report.
decisions.strongest_contrary_evidence: The strongest objection is that the numerical historical comparator actually used in the current distribution analysis (27.2% low, 67.6% medium, and mean 41.57 after rescaling 43.65/105 to 100) is the 2014 national sample already in Archer 2015 and reprinted in DeWitt 2016. The current paper does not separately tabulate a contrast with the targeted 2014-15 sample, and it does not repeat DeWitt 2016’s distinctive science-versus-cultural-capital prediction models or item-importance regressions; related hierarchical regressions are explicitly planned for future work. Thus the two journal publications and grouped Discussion citation alone would be insufficient. The additional original-specific evidence is DeWitt 2016’s independently reported targeted-sample distribution/demographic finding, which is inside the current paper’s explicitly attributed set-wide retest of younger cohorts. The lack of a separate targeted-sample statistical contrast does not cancel that conceptual empirical retest under Rule 2.

actual_empirical_retest.original_finding: In both the reused 2014 national survey and the distinct 2014-15 targeted survey, only a small minority have high science capital and it is concentrated among South Asian/Middle Eastern students, students with higher cultural capital, and top science sets. The targeted sample independently shows the low/high distribution and demographic pattern.
actual_empirical_retest.current_corresponding_analysis: The new age-17/18 survey’s low/medium/high distribution and ethnic/cultural-capital/science-set analyses retest those younger-cohort patterns; current Results expressly attributes the distribution to Author 2 2015 and Author 3 2016, and Discussion expressly places both in the retested set.
actual_empirical_retest.tested_finding_limits: No retest is inferred for the 2016 paper’s item-level beta rankings, its science-versus-cultural-capital predictive superiority, zoo-visitation coefficient or qualitative pen portraits. Merely using its instrument would not qualify.

identity.described_source: Recurring GSS welfare wording experiment; 2014 GSS ATE baseline and 2016 GSS race/ethnicity CATE comparison

decisions.rationale: Experiment 1 randomizes welfare versus assistance/caring for the poor wording and compares Lucid with both MTurk and the 2014 GSS. The heterogeneity section separately compares race/ethnicity effects against the 2016 GSS. The empirical relationship is established, but a specific published GSS paper or bibliographic dataset entry is not identified. For the named MTurk welfare finding, 2012 is represented. For the directly examined GSS baseline, identity remains unknown after complete current text/reference reading. Do not invent an earlier ancestor or add an unidentified paper merely because an experiment is real. This verdict is about candidate0.identity, not a claim that no welfare retest exists.
decisions.all_shipped_match_analysis: The MTurk comparison falls within retained row 462. Candidate 0 as assigned has blank citation fields and describes GSS, so it cannot be silently rebound to 2012 and called an independently identified GSS pair. No shipped GSS identity is present.
decisions.alternate_preliminary_reports: Gilens (1996), “Race coding” and white opposition to welfare, is cited for subsequent race-related welfare context, explicitly distinguished from the original wording experiment; it does not uniquely identify that experiment. Neither recurring GSS years nor the MTurk report provide a unique bibliographic identity for the GSS baseline. Candidate 0 overlaps row 462 only in the MTurk branch. Other candidates test distinct manipulations.

strongest_contrary_evidence.objection: The paper explicitly calls Experiment 1 a replication, and the 2012 paper offers a named intervening report for the same wording effect.
strongest_contrary_evidence.response: That supports retaining the 2012 pair and confirms actual welfare retesting. It does not identify the assigned GSS source or make 2012 an alternate report of the 2014/2016 GSS samples. Preserve the prior undeterminable-GSS-identity objection; revise only its template-only characterization of 2012.

identity.title: The framing of decisions and the psychology of choice.

decisions.rationale: Experiment 2 reruns the Asian Disease mortality/gain framing choice and explicitly compares average effects with the original undergraduate classroom sample as well as MTurk. The authors distinguish substantial effect magnitudes across samples while comparing direction and qualitative conclusions. Figure 2 uses the original experiment mean and SD as its scale. 2012 is the retested MTurk comparator, while 1981 is also a directly retested original-sample comparator: its finding, sample and differing magnitude are substantively evaluated. The older source is not retained merely because it originated the chain or supplied wording. The three-sample comparison supplies independent target evidence. Count each directly tested paper once, not each experimental arm.
decisions.all_shipped_match_analysis: No shipped Tversky–Kahneman pair exists. The sole 2012 pair reports a different MTurk sample and is not an alternative report of the original classroom data.
decisions.alternate_preliminary_reports: The 1981 Science paper is explicitly referenced as the finding source; no competing protocol, preliminary report or same-author alternative is named for this test. Candidate 2 concerns risk-acceptance moderation; Note 11 explicitly distinguishes that extension from the Asian Disease main framing experiment. Shared paradigm alone does not collapse those papers.

strongest_contrary_evidence.objection: Berinsky et al. (2012) already replicated the Asian Disease finding, making 1981 an ancestor under a closest-chain reading.
strongest_contrary_evidence.response: That would justify exclusion if the current paper tested only the MTurk result. Here it expressly includes the original classroom experiment in the empirical comparison and evaluates the effect magnitudes across all three samples. Keeping the direct original comparison alongside the MTurk report does not infer a target from citation alone.

decisions.rationale: Experiment 3 retests the risk-acceptance/risky-choice association and whether risk acceptance conditions the mortality-frame effect. Beyond comparing the MTurk finding with Lucid, the heterogeneity results explicitly compare the original Kam–Simas sample with Lucid and examine the absence of moderation in both. Note 10 establishes 2012 as the closest report of the MTurk replication actually tested. It does not erase the separately stated original-versus-Lucid CATE comparison. The original is retained on that empirical comparison, not solely on the heading “replicates Kam and Simas”. Both reports are actual comparators, so no single-chain-target substitution is warranted.
decisions.all_shipped_match_analysis: The sole shipped 2012 MTurk paper is a separate replication report, not Kam and Simas’s 2010 Journal of Politics paper or its original sample. Candidate 2 is absent from shipped pairs even after retaining 462.
decisions.alternate_preliminary_reports: The exact reference, Experiment 3 and Table 1 agree on Kam and Simas (2010). No alternative published/preliminary report is supplied for that original. Candidate 1 shares the disease task but not the risk-acceptance question; Note 11 makes the difference explicit. The new study of the MTurk replication and the direct original-sample CATE comparison overlap substantively without being the same paper identity.

strongest_contrary_evidence.objection: The complete risk-acceptance finding was already replicated in MTurk, and Note 10 links it to the 2012 report; the codebook warns against substituting the chain origin for the closest target.
strongest_contrary_evidence.response: Retain the 2012 target for that comparison. The original-versus-Lucid CATE passage separately tests the original sample’s absence of moderation, rather than merely reciting its intellectual lineage. Excluding 2010 would delete a directly reported empirical comparison.

identity.title: Through a glass and darkly: Attitudes toward international trade and the curious effects of issue framing.

decisions.rationale: Experiment 4 tests expert opinion and positive/negative trade frames in a 2 × 4 design. It compares frame estimates across all examined samples, explicitly mentions original and MTurk combined-frame estimates, and separately compares education and expert-treatment heterogeneity in original Hiscox and Lucid samples. The original definition of low education is expressly used. 2012 is a directly retested MTurk branch; Hiscox (2006) is a directly retested original branch. Most decisively, original-versus-Lucid education and randomly assigned expert-opinion heterogeneity are explicitly assessed beyond the generic method citation. No rule makes the mere presence of a 2012 estimate invalidate those original-specific tests.
decisions.all_shipped_match_analysis: No shipped Hiscox pair is present. The sole 2012 paper contains MTurk replication estimates, not the original Hiscox sample/report; its identity aliases cannot represent Hiscox’s 2006 International Organization article.
decisions.alternate_preliminary_reports: The reference-list title, author, year, 2 × 4 manipulation and education definition identify the primary Hiscox article. No alternative/preliminary version or protocol is cited for these data. It is separate from all other candidate experiments. Retaining 2012 preserves the MTurk benchmark without duplicating the original Hiscox report.

strongest_contrary_evidence.objection: The earlier MTurk replication used the same free-trade experiment, so 2012 could be the closest study for the shared framing finding. The sentence about combined positive/negative frames explicitly mentions original and MTurk, not Lucid.
strongest_contrary_evidence.response: The candidate is not inferred from that isolated sentence. The study names Hiscox as replicated, compares all examined samples, and directly examines original-versus-Lucid heterogeneity and the Hiscox education boundary. These establish the target independently of treating every MTurk result as a new Hiscox test.

identity.title: Rumors and health care reform: Experiments in political misinformation.

decisions.rationale: Experiment 5 reruns ACA death-panel rumor corrections, comparing Lucid in 2016 with the SSI sample collected in 2010 and reported by Berinsky (2017). It compares baseline rumor belief (−0.17 versus −0.19), correction effects and partisan conditional effects. Figure 5 labels original and Lucid, with no MTurk series. The closest actually tested source is Berinsky (2017), with its original 2010 SSI findings. There is no MTurk ancestor in this experiment according to the current paper. The 2012 target therefore neither absorbs nor replaces candidate 4.
decisions.all_shipped_match_analysis: The sole shipped 2012 three-author MTurk-validation paper is not the single-author 2017 healthcare-rumor report. Same first author does not create report equivalence. The current source explicitly says this experiment had not previously been replicated on MTurk.
decisions.alternate_preliminary_reports: The printed reference identifies the British Journal of Political Science paper. The 2010 data-collection year is not a competing published-paper identity. No alternate/preliminary 2012 report of these SSI results is supplied. This manipulation, dataset, corrections and partisan comparisons differ from all four other experiments.

strongest_contrary_evidence.objection: Berinsky is also the first author of the retained 2012 work, and the abstract presents the rumor exception in its general account of the Lucid validation exercise.
strongest_contrary_evidence.response: The results identify the 2017 experiment and its 2010 SSI sample; the experimental-comparison introduction explicitly excludes an MTurk ancestor. Author overlap and a whole-paper summary cannot establish the same report or chain. No outcome is assigned here.
